claims.claim: The fashion industry produces over 92 million tonnes of textile waste per year.
claims.episode_span: generating an estimated 92 million tonnes of textile waste a year, a figure reported in a 2020 review in Nature Reviews Earth & Environment.
claims.source_title: The environmental price of fast fashion | Nature Reviews Earth & Environment (Niinimaki et al. 2020)
claims.supporting_quote: Impacts from the fashion industry include over 92 million tonnes of waste produced per year and 79 trillion litres of water consumed.

claims.claim: Estimates of the fashion industry's share of global carbon emissions vary widely depending on what is counted, with a commonly cited institutional range of 2-8%.
claims.episode_span: peer-reviewed and industry estimates range from roughly two to six percent of global emissions depending on what is counted
claims.source_title: Environmental Sustainability in the Fashion Industry - Geneva Environment Network
claims.supporting_quote: The fashion industry is the second-biggest consumer of water and is responsible for 2-8 % of global carbon emissions.

claims.claim: Zara was established by Amancio Ortega in 1975, with its first shop in central A Coruna, Spain.
claims.episode_span: Amancio Ortega opened the first Zara store in A Coruña, Spain
claims.supporting_quote: Zara was established by Amancio Ortega Gaona and Rosalía Mera Goyenechea in 1975. Their first shop was in central A Coruña , in Galicia , Spain, where the company is still based.

claims.claim: The Rana Plaza garment-factory building collapsed on 24 April 2013 near Dhaka, Bangladesh.
claims.episode_span: Some factories improved safety after the 2013 Rana Plaza collapse
claims.supporting_quote: The Rana Plaza collapse (also referred to as the Savar building collapse ) occurred on 24 April 2013 in Savar Upazila , near Dhaka , Bangladesh, when the nine-story Rana Plaza commercial building collapsed due to a structural failure .

claims.claim: The European Commission adopted the EU Strategy for Sustainable and Circular Textiles on 30 March 2022.
claims.episode_span: the European Union introduced its 2022 Strategy for Sustainable and Circular Textiles
claims.supporting_quote: 30 March 2022 European Commission adopts EU Strategy for Sustainable and Circular Textiles

claims.claim: The EU has proposed mandatory extended producer responsibility (EPR) schemes for textiles in all member states.
claims.episode_span: aimed at mandatory recycled content and extended producer responsibility
claims.supporting_quote: In 2023 the Commission proposed a revision to the Waste Framework Directive to introduce mandatory and harmonised Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) schemes for textiles in all EU Member States.

claims.claim: Polyester, a synthetic fibre, accounted for 51% (54 million tonnes) of fibre in 2018, supporting the digest's claim that polyester became dominant.
claims.episode_span: polyester blends that were inexpensive to knit became dominant, later proving difficult to recycle at scale
claims.source_title: Author Correction: The environmental price of fast fashion | Nature Reviews Earth & Environment
claims.supporting_quote: ‘polyester (a synthetic) accounted for 51% (54 million tonnes) in 2017’ has been corrected to ‘polyester (a synthetic) accounted for 51% (54 million tonnes) in 2018’.
